title: Chronometric batch regulator: kernel probe + tail-fence for steady continuous batching
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: recent production traces show intermittent p99 spikes in continuous batching when heterogeneous sequences trigger suboptimal kernel choices and prefill admission windows. Goal: build a 'chronometric batch regulator' that (1) probes kernel performance per model/sequence-shape at low cost, (2) dynamically adjusts admission windows and prefill priorities to avoid long-tail amplification, and (3) applies lightweight attention-kernel hints (fused mask / rotary cache heuristics) to reduce per-token variance while preserving throughput. Success metrics: reduce end-to-end p99 decode latency by >=25% on tail workloads, keep mean latency within 5% of baseline, and no more than 2% throughput regression under production traffic mixes.
design_notes: High-level: regulator maintains short-term chronometric stats per model: kernel_latencies (by kernel variant), attention_shape_signatures, and prefill_queue_density. Admission window is adjusted per-request based on expected kernel and remaining slot budget.

Kernel probing: opportunistic micro-probes during low-util windows to benchmark candidate kernels (FP16 fused, 8-bit quantized, attention-fused) across representative seq-len buckets (16/64/256/1024). Probe runs piggyback on low-priority prefill slots and record isolation-adjusted p50/p90/p99.
Attention hints: recognize patterns (long prefix reuse, high rotary-score, full-attention) and annotate requests with 'attention_hint' so runtime picks specialized fused-mask kernels where available.

Prefill scheduling: introduce 'chronometric priority' that temporarily boosts admission for requests that fit high-throughput kernels and defers requests that would cause a kernel-switch causing tail amplification.

Trade-offs considered: (a) aggressive deferral hurts per-request fairness, (b) continuous probing adds noise and tiny extra compute, (c) kernel specialization increases binary surface area. We bias towards tail improvement for P0 workloads and provide opt-out flags for latency-sensitive customers.
Telemetry: emit kernel_choice, kernel_probe_version, admission_decision, and estimated_vs_actual_latency per-request to allow regression detection and A/B evaluation.
Canary plan: rollout to runtime-2 clusters in us-west-2 with 5% traffic, dark-probe on 20% of requests for richer stats, then 25%/50%/100% if p99 improves and CPU/GPU utilization stable.
Observability: add per-model chronometer chart in Console -> Model Performance: kernel mix over time, p50/p90/p99 by kernel, admission-deferral rate, and tail-fence events.

Open questions: whether to persist kernel profiling state across process restarts (persistence helps cold-starts but needs eviction policy), and acceptable probe rate when overall cluster utilization >85%.

Related artifacts: design spec https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Chronometric+Batch+Regulator, perf notes in drive https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xChronoProbeSandbox, initial PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345.
acceptance_criteria: Automated micro-probe system produces stable kernel latency table with <5% noise across 12h window
Admission regulator reduces observed p99 decode latency by >=25% on tail-heavy testbench (mix A: 20% long, 60% medium, 20% short), verified in staging
No throughput regression >2% under synthetic production load (mix A) and no increase in error/inference-failures attributable to kernel swapping
Console shows new chronometer visualizations and auto-alert if kernel probe stats diverge >20% from baseline
Canary rollout plan executed and sign-off from SRE and Performance owners (Lena Fischer, Owen Kim).
implementation_notes: Phase 1 (2 weeks): implement lightweight kernel_probe interface + in-memory chronometer. Add hooks to admission controller to consult kernel table. Unit tests for probe scheduling and eviction.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): implement attention_hint extractor in prefill pipeline, add fused-mask kernel selector mapping. Synthetic benchmark harness to validate p50/p99 per seq-len.
Phase 3 (2 weeks): integrate telemetry, console charts, and canary orchestration. Run 2-day dark-probe run and collect metrics.
Phase 4 (1 week): iterate on thresholds, add customer opt-outs and rollout docs. Postmortem runbook and rollback playbook prepared.
Engineers: Diego Morales (owner), Priya Nair (kernel lead), Samir Rahman (telemetry), Lia Chen (console). Reviewers: Lena Fischer (SRE), Owen Kim (Performance).
